`strategy:druckenmiller-liquidity` | confidence: **single-source** | tags: global, process, macro, position-sizing

Rules as described by Druckenmiller in interviews: (1) Earnings don't move the overall market; central banks and liquidity do - focus on the Fed (for India: RBI stance, system liquidity, FPI flows, the rupee and US real yields). (2) Look 18-24 months ahead; price action today reflects what investors expect then. (3) When several signals line up (liquidity, valuation, technicals/price confirmation), bet big - concentration, not diversification, is where returns come from. (4) Use price as information: if the market doesn't confirm the thesis, cut fast; preservation of capital comes first. (5) Change your mind without ego when the regime changes. Individual adaptation: a quarterly liquidity checklist (RBI repo direction, banking-system liquidity surplus/deficit, credit growth, FPI and DII flows, USD/INR trend) to tilt equity exposure; fewer, larger positions with explicit exit conditions. Failure mode: overconfidence and chasing at the top (his own 2000 tech buy). Evidence: his record is press-reported, not audited; treat this as a process template, not a proven formula for individuals.

Links: person:stanley-druckenmiller (about); strategy:position-sizing (similar_to)

Sources: <https://moneyweek.com/441992/the-worlds-greatest-investors-stanley-druckenmiller> ; <https://moiglobal.com/latticework-stanley-druckenmiller-202503>

`event:india-fpi-exodus-2025-26` | confidence: **verified** | tags: india, macro, policy, smallcap, base-rate, cyclical

Nifty peaked at ~26,277 on 27 Sept 2024 (from memory) and fell ~17% to ~21,700-22,000 by Mar-Apr 2025 (US tariff shock; from memory); the Nifty Smallcap 250 fell 24%+ from its Sept 2024 peak to 14,145 on 17 Feb 2025 and had its weakest calendar year in seven years in 2025 (-6 to -7%). Smallcap 250 TRI -24% vs Nifty 50 TRI -8% in the 2025 correction, still below its peak 18 months later (Mar 2026, DSP). FPIs sold a record ~Rs 1.66 lakh crore in 2025; 2026 then saw the US-Iran war (from 28 Feb 2026) and crude above $100: FPI outflows of ~Rs 1.68-1.92 lakh crore in Jan-Apr 2026, ~Rs 2.41 lakh crore for 2026 before November; FPI ownership of NSE firms fell to a 17-year low (~15.8%). The rupee breached 96/USD (record low ~96.5-97.2 in May 2026 per earlier memdb record) vs ~94.2 in mid-Nov. Domestic flows absorbed it: DII inflows ~Rs 8.5 lakh crore in FY26 and SIPs ~Rs 32,000 crore a month. Nifty ~23,700 on 22 May 2026; then recovery: record FPI buying of Rs 84,291 crore in the first half of Nov 2026, led by financials and autos; Nifty 25,228 and Sensex 82,032 on 18 Nov 2026. Valuation (Nov 2026): Nifty ~20.6x trailing; Smallcap 250 forward ~21.9x vs 18.7x average. Lesson: FPI selling plus a weak rupee hits small caps hardest; domestic SIP flows now cushion large caps; FPI capitulation (ownership at 17-year lows) preceded the turn.

| `base_rates.json` | The reference classes shown next to every probability, each with its source, biases, 95% CI and size band. `null` means no honest number on file. **v2 (2026-11-23):** `india_nonfin_1000_20000cr_5y` and `us_float_500m_10b_5y`, survivorship-free (method: `research_notes/Backtests/base_rates_5y.md`; script `tools/backtests/base_rates_5y/build.py`). Old classes keep a `_deprecated` suffix; an old card that names the old key resolves to it and prints "Deprecated class" |
| `calibration_2026-11-23/` | All 6 cards re-run with worksheet v1.3, card v1.1 and base rates v2 (no calls written). Results and reasons in its README: all 6 still size 0 |
| `examples/` | Cards for VMM, CUMMINSIND and US-FIVE (TEST MATERIAL, no verdict), plus a fictional SYNTHETIC card that exercises the path where every gate clears |

Card v1.1 (2026-11-23) adds three stage-5 lines when the worksheet has them: cash tax, reinvestment realism and
the exit-multiple bet (EV of the 5-year multiple at the stated exits, at the DCF-consistent P/E and at the own median).
It also prints base-rate CIs and the size-band warning, and applies the market-specific PEAD gate.

Bank/NBFC worksheets (`"mode": "bank"`, v1.1) are supported: the stage-5 block then reports reverse P/B, implied CoE,
residual-income scenarios, P/B temperature and book stress. Example: `examples/FEDERALBNK_card.json` (practice).

**Business.** One tertiary/quaternary hospital (Sarita Vihar, Mathura Road), ~700 beds `[EST: public descriptions; bed count NOT disclosed in AR24–26]`.
FY26: 63,236 discharges (−2%), ALOS 3.23 days (3.07), revenue per patient ₹2.25 lakh (+11%), 607k OPD visits (+2%), revenue per bed-day ₹69,714 (+6%)
`[AR26 MD&A]`. Occupied beds ≈ 204,252 ÷ 365 = **~560** `[EST]` → ~79% occupancy on ~700 beds `[EST, bed count unverified]`.
**Ownership and the PPP structure.** Founded 1988 "as a joint venture Company between the Govt. of NCT of Delhi and Apollo Hospitals Group … first
of its kind … public-private partnership" `[AR26 MD&A]`. Promoters 51.00% = GNCTD 26.00% + Apollo Hospitals Enterprise 22.45% + Reddy family/others
`[SHP XBRL 30-Sep-2026]`. Public 44.8% across 77,706 holders (up from 51,448 in Dec-2023); FIIs 2.4%, DIIs 1.8% `[SCR]`.
**The land (the key structural fact).** "The Hospital building has been constructed on the land leased out to the Company by the Government of
NCT of Delhi. The Government … has met the expenditure to the extent of ₹15.48 Crore … for construction of building … The ownership of the building
between Government of NCT of Delhi and the Company will be decided at a future date"; ground rent **₹12 per year** `[AR26 n.30.D]`. Net book value of
the building ₹127.2 cr. In return the lease requires free treatment for the poor (GNCTD: **one-third of IPD and 40% of OPD**) `[PRESS]`.
**Holdco/non-operating flag (v1.4):** net cash ₹521 cr = **16% of market cap** — below the 20% stub rule of thumb, but in a handover scenario it is
most of what is left.
**Cyclicality flag:** none (COVID FY21 was the only down year). The stock does screen cheap vs peers, so the "why cheap" test is in 8.2b.
**Peers:** Artemis Medicare (one Gurugram flagship; 44.3x), Shalby (33.3x), Yatharth (54.9x), Jupiter Life Line (51.3x), Narayana (44.6x),
Apollo Hospitals (58.8x) `[SCR 24-Nov-2026]`; median **48.0x**.
